recipes.name: Fermented pollock roe (Myeongnanjeot: 명란젓)
recipes.yield: About 2½ cups (a little more than 1 pound)
ingredients: 1 pound frozen or fresh pollock roe (If frozen, thaw it out in the fridge)
5 to 6 tablespoons gochugaru (Korean hot pepper flakes) for seasoning, plus 2 to 3 tablespoons for topping
instructions: Combine 4 cups cold water and 1 tablespoon kosher salt in a bowl and stir until dissolved. Add the pollock roe and gently wash it by hand, then put it into a strainer. Gently rinse and drain a few more times until very clean. Pat dry with a kitchen towel or paper towels. Remove any stringy material and discard. If any roe sacs are too big, gently split them into smaller pieces with your hands.

Combine 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon kosher salt, 5 to 6 tablespoons gochugaru (Korean hot pepper flakes), mirim, garlic, and ginger in a bowl and mix well with a spoon. Add the roe and gently mix to coat evenly. Transfer to a small earthenware or glass jar; this amount should fit into a 2½ cup jar. Spread 2 to 3 tablespoons gochugaru evenly over the top and gently press down with a spoon. Cover and refrigerate for 3 weeks to ferment.

Take 2 to 3 roe sacs out of the jar and slice them a few times on a cutting board. Put them in a small bowl or on a plate. Sprinkle with chopped green onion, toasted sesame oil, and toasted sesame seeds. Serve with rice, soup, and other side dishes.

ingredient_sections.text: Makes about 2½ cups (a little more than 1 pound) of myeongnanjeot:
Preparation time: about 20 minutes to wash, season, and pack the roe into a jar, plus 3 weeks for fermentation in the refrigerator.
1 pound frozen or fresh pollock roe (If frozen, thaw it out in the fridge)
5 to 6 tablespoons gochugaru (Korean hot pepper flakes) for seasoning, plus 2 to 3 tablespoons for topping
